gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Outdoor 4 takes outside power only through its USB-C socket, or that Blink says the camera 'is no longer weather-resistant' once the USB port cover is removed unless a weather-resistant USB-C adapter is used. It also doesn't state that Blink's Outdoor 4 Battery Extension Pack blocks that socket, so a separately mounted panel can't be used with the pack.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ, the cited Blink Solaris FAQ, Blink's 'How to Power your Blink Camera' page and Blink's Outdoor 4 Battery Extension Pack page. The Solar Panel Mount FAQ gives only part of the reason: the Outdoor 4 is 'NOT compatible with its Micro-USB connector' that provides 'a weather resistant seal'. It never names the Outdoor 4's own USB-C socket. The 'How to Power' page lists the Outdoor 4 among cameras powered 'by a micro USB cable', which contradicts Blink's Outdoor 4 page saying USB-C. The extension-pack page says the socket gets blocked but sits on a separate page and is never tied to solar. No rival page links the three facts: the socket is USB-C, removing its cover breaks weather resistance, and the pack blocks it. Also, the cited Solaris FAQ as read today names only the Outdoor 2K+, but ChatGPT told the shopper that Blink confirms the Outdoor 4.
decides: If the shopper wants a panel mounted apart from the camera, the deciding question is how well the plug seals the Outdoor 4's USB-C socket. Blink calls for a 'weather resistant USB-C adapter'. Wasserstein's panel uses a micro-USB cable plus a 'USB C converter'. Its listing calls the cable 'weatherproof' but says nothing about the converter joint, so the page should flag that seal. A shopper who already uses the Battery Extension Pack has to remove it before any USB-C solar panel will fit. For Solaris, Blink's own Solaris FAQ and setup guide currently name only the Outdoor 2K+, while retailers still list it 'for Outdoor 4'. The page should stop saying 'Blink confirms Outdoor 4' and cite only the retailer wording until Blink lists the Outdoor 4 again.

findings.label: External power input and weather seal
findings.value: USB-C port; 'The Outdoor 4 can be powered through its USB-C port using a weather resistant USB-C adapter; however, once the USB port cover is removed, the camera is no longer weather-resistant until it's reinserted.'
findings.source_title: How to install batteries on Outdoor 4 camera — Blink Support
findings.note: Maker's own wording, quoted exactly. Any separately mounted panel has to plug into this socket, so the plug has to do the weather sealing.

findings.label: Battery type
findings.value: 'Blink cameras are only compatible with size AA 1.5 volt Lithium non-rechargeable batteries.'
findings.source_title: How to install batteries on Outdoor 4 camera — Blink Support
findings.note: The camera's own cells can't be recharged, so a panel has to supply the power itself (from its own battery at night) rather than top up the AAs.

findings.label: Blocks the USB-C socket

findings.source_title: Installing Outdoor 4 Battery Extension Pack — Blink Support
findings.note: The extension pack and a USB-C solar panel can't be used together.

findings.source_title: Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ — Blink Support
findings.note: The mount's sealed connector is micro-USB and the Outdoor 4 socket is USB-C.
